clue.text: State lead over posh bar out of town

parts.note: a state is a country

indicators.note: the lead sits over the posh letter, covering it on both sides in this down clue

parts.note: Pb is the chemical symbol for lead
U is the old label for upper-class, posh usage

explanation.surface: Someone states their preference: a smart bar away from the city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lead' is the metal, not a leash or the front: its symbol PB goes 'over' U to make PUB.
explanation.definitionFit: A pub in a rural village is a drinking bar located outside any town.

clue.text: Less generous member of Wasps, say, inspires one

indicators.note: to inspire is literally to breathe in, so the stinger takes the letter into itself

parts.note: a stinger is the sting, a body part (member) of a wasp; 'Wasps' is also a rugby club, and 'say' flags the example
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A player from the Wasps rugby club motivates a teammate but is tight with money.
explanation.walkthrough: Wasps is an English rugby club, so 'member' reads as a player; really it is the insect's body part.
explanation.definitionFit: Stingy means mean with money; the comparative describes someone who gives even less.

clue.text: Work hard in Test to win prize

indicators.note: the work and hard letters are placed in the word for test

parts.note: to try is to test
op, short for opus, is a work
H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils

explanation.surface: A cricketer must graft in a Test match to win the trophy.
explanation.definitionFit: A trophy such as a cup is awarded as a prize to a winner.

clue.text: Check rule, having lost golf

indicators.note: the word for rule has lost the letter for golf, so it is removed

parts.note: a monarch's reign is their rule
G is golf in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A golfer who has lost should check their temper and their rule-keeping.
explanation.definitionFit: To rein in is to restrain, and a rein is a check on movement.

clue.text: Clean medical department, bandaging artery first

indicators.note: bandaging wraps round, so the word for clean is placed around the artery

parts.note: a bird preens, cleaning its feathers
the M1 is a main road artery of England; the 1 is read as I
ENT is the ear, nose and throat department of a hospital

explanation.surface: A hospital department must be clean, and a bleeding artery gets bandaged before anything else.
explanation.walkthrough: 'artery' looks medical but is a major road: the M1, with the figure 1 standing as the letter I.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone pre-eminent stands above all rivals, so they come first.

clue.text: Amateur regularly left wrong score in the Open

indicators.note: taking letters at regular intervals from the word left gives its first and third
wrong signals that the letters of score are set out in an incorrect order

explanation.surface: An amateur golfer at the Open championship regularly records a wrong score.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the Open' is a golf championship in the surface; really it means outdoors. 'regularly' picks LF from 'left'; 'wrong' turns SCORE into RESCO.
explanation.definitionFit: Alfresco means outdoors, in the open air.

clue.text: Nothing's shown up in extra writer's ID

indicators.note: the turned word is put in the word for extra

parts.note: a bye is an extra run in cricket

indicators.note: in a down clue, being shown up means the word for nothing is read bottom to top

parts.note: nil is nothing; the 's stands for is, a link

explanation.surface: A journalist complains that nothing identifies them in a newspaper's extra edition.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shown up' turns NIL into LIN, which goes 'in' BYE, a cricket extra.
explanation.definitionFit: A byline is the line naming the author of a newspaper article, identifying the writer.

clue.text: Game's up! Sell!

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the game's name is read from the bottom

parts.note: golf is a game; the 's stands for is, a link

explanation.surface: The game is over, someone shouts: time to sell up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Game's up' sounds like defeat, but 'up' turns GOLF over in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Flog is British slang for selling something.

clue.text: Overall, we are mad to cut foreign tour

indicators.note: the second jumble cuts into the first, sitting inside it
something foreign is strange or unfamiliar, so the letters of tour are made strange by rearranging
mad suggests the letters of we are go wild and change order

explanation.surface: On the whole, a group declares itself mad to curtail a trip abroad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Overall' looks like 'on the whole' but is the garment. Both 'foreign' and 'mad' signal jumbles, and 'to cut' puts the second inside the first.
explanation.definitionFit: An overall is a protective coat worn over clothes, a kind of outer garment.

clue.text: Left old university? Not entirely true

indicators.note: the university's name is not given in full, losing its last letter

parts.note: Yale is a university in the USA

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a person really left their old university, doubting it is fully true.
explanation.definitionFit: A loyal friend is faithful, and true is an old sense of faithful.

clue.text: Six Counties writer bowled over by Peg in lane

parts.note: the Six Counties is a name for Northern Ireland, abbreviated NI

indicators.note: bowled over means knocked flat and turned, so the writer is read backwards

parts.note: a pen is a writer
by can mean in, as in 'by day' meaning in the day

explanation.surface: A Northern Irish author is overwhelmed by a woman called Peg in a lane.
explanation.walkthrough: Peg looks like a woman's name; it is a skittle standing in a bowling lane. 'bowled over' turns PEN into NEP.
explanation.definitionFit: A ninepin is one of the skittles, a wooden pin set up at the end of a bowling alley.

clue.text: What students want to be studying, having dropped Latin?

indicators.note: the word for studying has dropped the letter for Latin, so it is removed

parts.note: studying is learning

explanation.surface: A wry question about what students would rather be doing once Latin is off the syllabus.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as a whole question; the definition is only its opening, and 'to be' links.
explanation.definitionFit: Hard-up students want income, so they want to be paid for work rather than studying.

clue.text: Wet track limits Asians every so often

indicators.note: the track letters form the limits, around the picked letters

parts.note: RY is the abbreviation for railway, a track

indicators.note: every so often means taking the letters at intervals, the first, third and fifth

explanation.surface: A rain-soaked running track occasionally holds up Asian athletes.
explanation.definitionFit: A rainy day is a wet one, with rain falling.

clue.text: Seamen hit rocks, struggling with this?

indicators.note: rocks means shakes about, so the letters of the two words are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: Sailors strike rocks while battling with their sails.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rocks' looks like the hazard they hit, but it is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: The mainsheet is the rope controlling a yacht's mainsail, which crews often battle in strong wind.

clue.text: Dull detail about champion's final exchange?

indicators.note: the two words go about the champion's letters, which sit between them

parts.note: a matt (also mat) finish is dull
a point is a detail, as in a point of law

explanation.surface: A boring point about a champion's decisive rally in the final.
explanation.walkthrough: 'final' looks like a tournament final; the definition is the last rally of a match, with '?' flagging the play on 'exchange'.
explanation.definitionFit: Match point is the rally that can end a tennis match, its last exchange of shots.

clue.text: Secure roller that produces result in court

parts.note: to tie is to secure
a breaker is a large wave, also called a roller

explanation.surface: A sturdy roller is used on a tennis court to get it ready for a match.
explanation.walkthrough: 'court' looks legal; it is a tennis court, where a tie-breaker decides a set.
explanation.definitionFit: In tennis a tie-break settles a set level at six games, giving a result.

clue.text: Average salmon caught as menu item?

parts.note: a par (also parr) is a young salmon
a fish caught to be served as a course of a meal is caught for the course

explanation.surface: A salmon is caught to be served as a dish on the menu.
explanation.walkthrough: PAR is a recognised spelling of PARR, the young salmon, so the letters come straight from the fish.
explanation.definitionFit: Par is the standard golf score, so 'par for the course' is an idiom for normal or typical.

clue.text: Obscure cricket side, Irish, impresses head office

parts.note: the on side is the leg side of a cricket field

indicators.note: to impress is to press into, so the Irish word takes the office letters inside it

parts.note: Erse is the Irish Gaelic language

explanation.surface: An unknown Irish cricket team makes an impression on the bosses at headquarters.
explanation.definitionFit: A one-horse town is small and insignificant, little known.

clue.text: Better game allowed to get in the way

indicators.note: the allowed word gets in the way, sitting inside it

parts.note: a route is the way to go
let means allowed

explanation.surface: Someone argues a superior game is allowed to obstruct.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Better' reads as 'superior' but means one who bets.
explanation.definitionFit: Roulette is a casino gambling game, played by punters who bet.

clue.text: Covering spinner for one that's heading off

parts.note: a spinner is one kind of cricket bowler

indicators.note: heading off removes the head, the first letter of that

explanation.surface: A spin bowler gets ready to leave the field.
explanation.walkthrough: A spinner is a cricket bowler; and a bowler hat, a covering, goes on the head, which is the joke behind 'heading'.
explanation.definitionFit: A bowler hat is a round felt hat, a covering for the head.

clue.text: Opening's briefly unpleasant in rain

indicators.note: the shortened word goes in the word for rain

parts.note: rain is wet weather

indicators.note: briefly means cut short, losing the last letter

parts.note: icky is informal for unpleasant

explanation.surface: An opening batsman briefly faces a nasty spell in the rain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Opening' suggests cricket's opener; it is a wicket gate, a small door or gap.
explanation.definitionFit: A wicket is a small gate or door, an opening set in a larger one.

clue.text: More devoted trustee admits regret

indicators.note: admits means lets in, so the trustee's letters take the regret word inside

parts.note: to rue is to regret

explanation.surface: A more faithful trustee owns up to regrets.
explanation.definitionFit: True means loyal, so truer is more loyal or faithful.

clue.text: Recommend Lion maybe for game once

parts.note: to tip is to recommend
a lion is an example of a big cat

explanation.surface: Someone recommends a lion, perhaps, for an old-fashioned game.
explanation.definitionFit: Tipcat is an old children's game in which a tapered stick is struck and hit.

clue.text: High wind in game cramping current cricket club

indicators.note: cramping means confining, so the game's letters hold the others inside

parts.note: polo is a game played on horseback
I is the symbol for electric current

explanation.surface: A strong wind during a polo match hampers a nearby cricket club.
explanation.walkthrough: 'High wind' is not a gale: it is a high-pitched wind instrument.
explanation.definitionFit: The piccolo is a small flute, the highest-pitched woodwind in an orchestra.

clue.text: As a unit, Wolves press forwards

definitions.meaning: wolves acting together as a unit form a ...
in rugby the forwards are called the ...

explanation.surface: Wolverhampton Wanderers, nicknamed Wolves, push forward together as a team.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wolves' reads as the football club; here it is the animals.
explanation.definitionFit: Pack covers a group of wolves, compressing things, and a rugby team's forwards.

clue.text: PA tried various fliers

indicators.note: various suggests different forms, so the letters are put in a new order

explanation.surface: A personal assistant tried various leaflets.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fliers' looks like leaflets or pilots; it is insects.
explanation.definitionFit: Diptera is the insect order of two-winged flies, which fly.

clue.text: County academic keeps 20

indicators.note: keeps means holds within, so the academic's letters hold the other

parts.note: a don is a university academic
20 refers to the answer WICKET, which cricket scoring abbreviates as W

explanation.surface: A county's academic keeps a cricket wicket.
explanation.walkthrough: COUNTY DOWN is one of the six counties of Northern Ireland.
explanation.definitionFit: Down is a county of Northern Ireland, so it is an example of a county.

clue.text: It entails taking men on board, ending with mate

definitions.text: It entails taking men on board, ending with mate

parts.words: It entails taking men on board, ending with mate
parts.note: reads like a ship taking on crew, with a ship's mate, but describes capturing pieces on a board game until checkmate

explanation.surface: A ship takes on crew, finally signing up a mate.
explanation.definitionFit: In this board game players capture the opponent's pieces, called men, until checkmate ends it.

clue.text: Magpies making latest move in 24

parts.note: new means latest
castling is a move in chess, the answer to 24

explanation.surface: Birds make their newest move in a game.
explanation.walkthrough: The Magpies is the nickname of Newcastle United, an English football club.
explanation.definitionFit: Newcastle United's nickname is the Magpies, from their black-and-white strip.
